name: Clean Air Act "major source" emission thresholds by pollutant and area classification
description: Whether a stationary source (a factory, plant, or facility) needs a federal Title V or PSD/nonattainment-NSR air permit turns on whether its potential to emit crosses a tons-per-year (tpy) threshold, and the single definition in 40 CFR 70.2 sets a different number for each of three overlapping tests: the section 112 hazardous-air-pollutant test (10 tpy single HAP / 25 tpy combined), the section 302 major-stationary-source test (100 tpy of any regulated pollutant, or 100,000 tpy CO2e for greenhouse gases), and the section 182/188 nonattainment-area test, which is tiered by pollutant (VOC, NOx, CO, PM-10) and by how severely out of attainment the area is classified (Marginal/Moderate down to 100 tpy, Serious down to 50 tpy, Severe down to 25 tpy, Extreme down to 10 tpy for ozone precursors). A facility just under one threshold and just over another is a real, consequential distinction that the single defined term 'major source' hides. Each record is one pollutant/test/classification combination and its threshold. Answers 'what's the major-source threshold for VOC in a Severe ozone nonattainment area', 'does 25 tpy of a HAP make me major', 'what's the PSD threshold for a new pollutant'.

records.pollutant: any combination of such hazardous air pollutants
records.definition_heading: Major source means any stationary source
records.source_quote: For pollutants other than radionuclides, any stationary source or group of stationary sources located within a contiguous area and under common control that emits or has the potential to emit, in the aggregate, 10 tons per year (tpy) or more of any hazardous air pollutant which has been listed pursuant to section 112(b) of the Act, 25 tpy or more of any combination of such hazardous air pollutants, or such lesser quantity as the Administrator may establish by rule.

records.pollutant: any air pollutant subject to regulation
records.definition_heading: Major source means any stationary source
records.source_quote: A major stationary source of air pollutants, as defined in section 302 of the Act, that directly emits, or has the potential to emit, 100 tpy or more of any air pollutant subject to regulation (including any major source of fugitive emissions of any such pollutant, as determined by rule by the Administrator).

records.definition_heading: Major source means any stationary source
records.source_quote: Greenhouse gases (GHGs), the air pollutant defined in <https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/section-86.1818-12#p-86.1818-12(a)> § 86.1818-12(a) of this chapter as the aggregate group of six greenhouse gases: carbon dioxide, nitrous oxide, methane, hydrofluorocarbons, perfluorocarbons, and sulfur hexafluoride, shall not be subject to regulation unless, as of July 1, 2011, the GHG emissions are at a stationary source emitting or having the potential to emit 100,000 tpy CO 2 equivalent emissions.
